chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Al-Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man upon whom the prayers of the year had accumulated due to illness. He (peace be upon him) said: He does not need to make them up.

key_terms.صَلَاةُ السَّنَةِ: The prayers of the year (accumulated daily prayers over a year)
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He makes up / fulfills (the missed obligation)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to make up missed prayers if I was sick for a long time?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that prolonged illness exempts a believer from the burden of making up missed daily prayers, reflecting the Shia principle of *rukhas* (divine concessions) during incapacity. This ruling distinguishes between temporary absences requiring *qada* and chronic conditions where the obligation is lifted, emphasizing ease (*yusr*) in Islamic jurisprudence. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith through figures like Safwan and al-Is ibn Qasim.

en.hubeali: A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan, from Al Ays Bin Al Qasim who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man upon whom the (lapse) Sunnah Salāts have been accumulated due to illness’. Heasws said: ‘He would not (need to) fulfil’.
en.sarwar: 6. A group has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from al-‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man upon whom Salah (prayer) for one year has accumulated because of illness. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is not required to perform such Salah (prayer).”’
